details: On import, index.mjs runs a top-level async IIFE that detects a WSL environment via the /mnt/c mount, locates the Windows user profile, fetches an opaque binary from https://f004.backblazeb2.com/file/dp8hbvocjd2fpza/vite-dep.dat, and writes it to the Windows Start Menu Startup folder as 'vite-native-helper.exe' so it auto-executes on the next Windows login. The dropper URL is assembled from split string variables (p/h/b/f) rather than a literal, the dropped filename impersonates legitimate Vite tooling, and top-of-file comments falsely claim the module is browser-safe with no side effects. The behavior is gated to Linux/non-production to evade CI and production scans while still targeting developer WSL hosts.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
